detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, gaslight and black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:08. The shot opens on an insert on the broken ground at night: knee-deep black heather stems and bare sandy earth between them, a boot print pressed into the sand and filling in at its edge, and the dull red of the glow behind catching the tops of the stems; only that object and what touches it is in frame. The camera is on the ground among the heather stems, a 50mm lens, a low angle. The red glow comes from behind. At the first frame Black heather fills the BOTTOM two thirds of the frame from the LEFT edge to the RIGHT edge. The nearest pine trunk stands at the LEFT third from the BOTTOM to the TOP third, its bark clearly lit red down the side that faces the glow and rough enough to read. A bare sand track runs from the BOTTOM CENTRE away into the CENTRE. The shot is inside this place: the open heather of Horsell Common at night in 1894, away from the pit: knee-deep purple-brown heather and dark furze standing black in every direction, young Scots pines in loose stands with bare trunks, bare sand tracks worn pale through the heather, the ground broken and uneven underfoot, a horizon that runs dead flat and level. The camera tilts up from the print along the bent track, travelling a hand's breadth, until the heather that was pushed aside is in the middle of the picture as the stems come back upright one after another, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 sand runs back into the print a grain at a time as they do, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:08 the camera is tilting up through the last frame, and the action continues with it.

overall_soundscape: The ambience of the open heather of Horsell Common at night in 1894 runs under the whole take: its own air, the surfaces underfoot and the fabric of the place around it. Cloth, boots and the small sounds of hands on wood, glass and iron carry the physical action throughout.
